correctness.rationale: Scaling f_i=e_i/a_i gives the claimed c_i. A relation among the squares satisfies lambda_i=-c_(i-1)lambda_(i-1); its solution space is zero or one dimensional, and any nonzero solution has full support. This gives the determinant criterion and independence of any two squares for n≥3. The image of multiplication by a natural vector is one dimensional: nondegeneracy makes its own square nonzero and it annihilates all other vectors of that basis. In the displayed basis its image is the span of the squares in its support, so it must be supported on one coordinate. Isomorphisms are therefore monomial, and matching directed successor terms forces a rotation; matching the normalized loops makes every scalar 1. This argument is unchanged over field extensions. Any nonzero ideal contains a square by multiplication with a coordinate vector; the successor term propagates membership to all squares. Thus every nonzero ideal contains E², which has codimension one exactly on the singular locus. For finite fields a fixed block repeated e=n/d times has singular product iff its block product is an e-th root of (-1)^n. Such a root exists (use (-1)^d), so there are gcd(e,q-1) choices, including in characteristic 2. Burnside counts all rotations, Möbius inversion extracts minimum periods, and each orbit with minimum period m has size m and stabilizer C_(n/m). The constant necklaces leave exactly Q-gcd(n,Q) simple classes; this includes Q=1, when none exist.
residual_risks: The recorded finite tests are supplementary. The unrestricted and extension-field conclusions rest on the rank and ideal arguments, not on those tests.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Diagonal similarity preserves matrix diagonal entries and rescales the successor weights by ratios of diagonal entries of the conjugator; this is not the quadratic change of basis in an algebra product. For instance on constant loop coefficient 1, diagonal similarity of the matrices retains just the full successor product, while algebra isomorphism retains the entire successor necklace. Removing the loops also removes the equation forcing the scalar factors to be 1. Neither comparator is an equivalent parameterization.

value.rationale: The family is the sparse directed cycle with both loop and successor terms nonzero, a natural setting in which distinct squared basis vectors stay independent even as perfection fails. Knowing the exact unique proper ideal at degeneration and the number of classes at each automorphism order gives concrete information unavailable from mere existence of a realization. In particular the exact full-symmetry simple count decides realizability in this family over very small finite fields. This is a complete joint census of the stated family, not a choice of a few sample fields or a claim of novelty for unrestricted necklace enumeration.
residual_risks: The result is about ordinary linear automorphisms in the looped-cycle family, not semilinear maps, automorphism group schemes or arbitrary support digraphs.
